recommendation: In this fictional scenario, run a bounded three-week prototype validation focused on preserving decision state with less upkeep than manual ledgers.
why: One qualified fictional Lead User episode demonstrates sustained high benefit from reducing handoff reconstruction.
The independent abandonment case makes maintenance burden a decisive design and validation constraint.
Derivative adoption cannot be counted as independent confirmation.
critical_uncertainties: Whether a lower-maintenance mechanism can preserve enough decision context to create net benefit
Whether the need appears across independent real operators

action_now.action: Run a fictional three-week prototype validation of two handoff mechanisms
action_now.deliverable: A comparison of handoff recovery value, upkeep cost, and failure modes for M1 and M2
evidence_to_collect: Minutes spent preparing and recovering each handoff
Decisions or constraints lost, repeated, or incorrectly revived
Differences across at least three independent workflow lineages
action_now.success_condition: At least one mechanism reduces total handoff effort by 50% without increasing consequential decision loss relative to the current approach
action_now.stop_condition: Stop if neither mechanism produces net time benefit after two consecutive observed handoffs or if consequential context loss increases
action_now.decision_at_end: Choose ACT, HOLD, or REJECT for a real discovery investment; do not select a production mechanism from this synthetic fixture

change_conditions: Move toward ACT only if independent real operators show net benefit after maintenance cost and no increase in consequential context loss.
Move to REJECT if low-maintenance mechanisms repeatedly lose critical decisions or remain net-costly.
what_evidence_supports: The fictional need is plausible enough to justify a bounded validation test.
Maintenance burden belongs in the fitness conditions.
what_evidence_does_not_support: Any claim about real users, prevalence, market size, willingness to pay, or production feasibility
Selection of M1 or M2 as a production product solution; M1 is selected only as a fictional prototype-comparison arm
contradictions: The independent counterexample shows that a handoff artifact can cost more to maintain than it saves.
The second adoption is derivative and supplies no independent benefit evidence.
recommended_next_evidence: For a real study, observe live handoffs among independently recruited multi-agent operators.
priority_human_review: Review whether LU1's fictional benefit signal would be strong enough for the intended real decision.
Review whether the maintenance-cost counterexample should block rather than shape concept work.
